title: The Lost Property Dragon
hook: Sami's lost rabbit is waiting in a secret office, and so is someone else.
blurb: Sami has lost Rabbit, and he has looked everywhere. Then, at midnight, a label slides under his door, and the cupboard under the stairs starts to glow. Inside is the Lost Property Office, where every lost thing waits to be found, and where a small, fussy, knitted dragon called Ember keeps the rules. One thing per visitor. Rules are rules. But Ember has a label of his own, and Sami knows exactly who has been missing him for sixty years.
coverAlt: Sami in pyjamas with a torch, standing in a vast room of shelves full of umbrellas and odd socks, face to face with a small red knitted dragon in half-moon glasses

narrator.notes: Warm and storytelling, with gentle comedy for Ember's fussy rules (a squeaky, precise little voice). Page 7 tender and slow. Nani's line on page 9 soft and sleepy. The last page calm and unhurried.

style: Premium contemporary picture-book illustration: soft painterly 3D look, rounded expressive characters, warm lamp-light and torchlight against deep blue night, gentle film grain, cosy British terraced-house interiors, rich but uncluttered compositions, cinematic depth of field. Consistent characters on every page. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, signs or captions anywhere in the image; labels and notices are always blank.
world: Sami's family home: a narrow British terraced house at night, with a steep carpeted staircase and a small wooden cupboard door under the stairs. Through that door, by magic, is the Lost Property Office: an enormous, warm, dusty hall like an old railway station, with wooden shelves rising up into darkness, sliding ladders, and shelves crammed with umbrellas, single mittens, odd socks, scarves, a trombone, an empty goldfish bowl, a wedding hat, a cricket bat, and jars of keys. Brass lamps give pools of amber light. A tiny wooden desk with a tiny lamp sits in the middle of the floor. Every lost thing has a blank brown paper label tied on with string.

cast.name: Sami
cast.look: Sami: a 6-year-old boy with warm brown skin, short thick black hair with a tuft that always sticks up at the crown, big brown eyes and a round, expressive face. Wears navy-blue pyjamas printed with small orange rockets and bare feet. Often carries a chunky yellow torch.

cast.name: Nani
cast.look: Nani: a small, soft, elderly Bangladeshi woman with warm brown skin, kind crinkly eyes, silver-grey hair in a low bun, a little gold stud in one nostril, wearing a lilac cardigan over a long cream cotton tunic and loose trousers. In bed she wears a pale lilac nightdress.

cast.name: Ember
cast.role: A knitted dragon, Keeper of Lost Things
cast.look: Ember: a small hand-knitted toy dragon that has come to life, only a little taller than Rabbit, made of slightly faded bright-red wool with visible knitted stitches. Two little crooked yellow felt wings, a row of soft orange felt spikes down his back and tail, round black button eyes with stitched worried eyebrows, a round tummy, and a pair of tiny gold half-moon spectacles perched on his snout. When startled, small harmless puffs of orange sparks come from his nostrils.

cast.name: Rabbit
cast.look: Rabbit: Sami's well-loved soft toy rabbit, pale grey plush, slightly squashed, with long ears (the left ear chewed and floppy at the tip), black button eyes, a pink stitched nose and a faded blue ribbon round its neck. A toy: it never moves on its own.

pages.heading: Lost
pages.text:
Sami had lost Rabbit.

He had looked under the bus seats and behind the sofa. He had looked in the washing machine, twice.

"Lost things go somewhere," said Nani, tucking him in. "Sometimes they wait for us."

On the fridge downstairs was Nani's oldest photo. It showed Nani when she was six, hugging a small red knitted dragon.

"What happened to him?" Sami had asked once.

"I lost him on a train," Nani had said. "A long, long time ago."
pages.imageAlt: Nani tucking a sad Sami into bed, with an empty space on the pillow where Rabbit should be

art.shot: Medium view of the bed from the doorway, warm lamp-light.
art.prompt: Nani sits on the edge of Sami's bed, tucking the duvet around him and stroking his hair. Sami lies looking sadly at the empty dent on his pillow where Rabbit usually sleeps. A chunky yellow torch lies on the bedside table. Cosy small bedroom, bedside lamp glowing amber, deep blue night at the window. Tender and a little sad.

pages.heading: A Label Under the Door
pages.text:
At midnight, something slid under Sami's bedroom door.

It was a brown paper label, the kind you tie on a suitcase. In tiny curly writing it said: Found. One rabbit. Grey. One chewed ear. Please collect before morning.

On the back was an arrow.

Sami picked up his torch. The button was wobbly, so he had to hold it down with his thumb.

He followed the arrow down the stairs, to the little cupboard underneath them.

The cupboard door was glowing round the edges.
pages.imageAlt: Sami with his torch at the bottom of the stairs, staring at the cupboard door glowing round its edges

art.shot: From behind Sami at the foot of the stairs, looking at the cupboard door.
art.prompt: Sami stands at the bottom of the dark staircase in his rocket pyjamas, holding a blank brown paper label on a string in one hand and his yellow torch in the other, its beam on the small wooden cupboard door under the stairs. Warm golden light glows around all four edges of the cupboard door, as if something magical is inside. Curious, magical, not scary.

pages.heading: The Lost Property Office
pages.text:
Sami opened the door.

Instead of coats and the hoover, there was a room as big as a railway station. Shelves went up and up into the dark. They were full of umbrellas, odd socks and single mittens. There was a trombone, an empty goldfish bowl and about a thousand keys.

At a tiny desk sat a tiny dragon.

He was red, and knitted, and wore half-moon glasses. When he saw Sami, he jumped, and a puff of sparks came out of his nose.

"Name?" he squeaked. "Lost item? Please don't touch the umbrellas."
pages.imageAlt: A vast hall of shelves full of lost things, with a tiny knitted dragon jumping in surprise at his desk as Sami walks in

art.shot: Wide, from just inside the cupboard door, showing the huge hall.
art.prompt: Sami steps through the small cupboard door into an enormous warm hall of towering wooden shelves that disappear up into darkness, crammed with umbrellas, odd socks, mittens, a trombone, an empty goldfish bowl and jars of keys, each with a blank brown label. Brass lamps make pools of amber light. In the middle of the floor at a tiny wooden desk, Ember the small red knitted dragon jumps in surprise, his half-moon spectacles askew, a little puff of orange sparks from his nose. Awe and wonder, funny.

pages.heading: Rules Are Rules
pages.text:
The dragon was called Ember, and he was the Keeper of Lost Things.

He pointed to a board of rules. "Rule one, no running. Rule two, no crying on the umbrellas, they go rusty. Rule three, one thing per visitor. That one's very important."

"Why?" asked Sami.

Ember thought about it. "I'm not sure," he admitted. "But I made it up a long time ago, and rules are rules."

He climbed a very tall ladder. At the very top, between a wedding hat and a cricket bat, sat Rabbit.
pages.imageAlt: Ember climbing a very tall ladder towards Rabbit on the top shelf, while Sami watches from below

art.shot: Looking up the tall ladder from Sami's position on the floor.
art.prompt: Ember the small knitted dragon climbs a very tall wooden sliding ladder against the towering shelves, wings flapping for balance, spectacles slipping. Near the top, on a shelf between a big floppy wedding hat and a cricket bat, sits Rabbit the grey toy rabbit with one chewed ear. Sami stands far below at the foot of the ladder, shining his yellow torch upwards. A blank wooden noticeboard leans against the desk. Funny and hopeful.

pages.heading: Found
pages.text:
Ember carried Rabbit down. It took a long time, because Rabbit was nearly as big as he was.

Sami hugged Rabbit so hard that Rabbit's chewed ear flopped right over Sami's nose.

"You must love giving things back," said Sami.

Ember smiled a small smile. "I do. But hardly anyone comes. Most things just wait." He looked up at the shelves. "Some have waited a very long time."

Sami's torch flickered. He pressed the wobbly button, and the light swung across Ember's foot.

There was a label tied to it.
pages.imageAlt: Sami hugging Rabbit tightly as his torch beam lands on a label tied to Ember's foot

art.shot: Medium close view at floor level beside the tiny desk.
art.prompt: Sami kneels on the floor hugging Rabbit tightly with both arms, eyes shut with relief. His yellow torch, held loosely, sends a beam across the floor that lands on Ember's knitted foot, where an old, soft, blank brown paper label is tied on with string. Ember stands beside the desk, looking up wistfully at the endless shelves. Warm amber lamp-light. Tender, with a hint of mystery.

pages.heading: Ember's Label
pages.text:
The label was old and brown and soft at the edges.

It said: Found. One dragon. Red, knitted. Left on the 6:15 train.

"You're lost property too," said Sami.

Ember's wings drooped. "I waited and waited," he said. "Nobody came. So I made myself useful. Someone has to look after the lost things."

Sami looked at the red wool and the crooked little wings. He thought about the photo on the fridge.

"I know who lost you," he whispered. "She's asleep upstairs. And she still talks about you."
pages.imageAlt: Sami crouching to read the old label on Ember's foot as Ember's little wings droop

art.shot: Close two-shot, Sami crouched down to Ember's height.
art.prompt: Sami crouches down to Ember's height, Rabbit tucked under one arm, gently holding up the old blank brown label tied to Ember's foot and looking at the little dragon with dawning realisation. Ember's crooked felt wings droop and his stitched eyebrows are sad and hopeful at once. Soft pool of lamp-light in the vast dim hall. Emotional and gentle.

pages.heading: Rule Three
pages.text:
Ember's sparks went pink with happiness. Then they went grey.

"Rule three," he said quietly. "One thing per visitor."

Sami looked at Rabbit. Rabbit looked back at Sami, as much as a rabbit with button eyes can.

Sami had waited one day for Rabbit.

Nani had waited sixty years for Ember.

Sami took a deep breath. He put Rabbit gently down on the desk.

"I choose Ember," he said.
pages.imageAlt: Sami gently setting Rabbit down on Ember's tiny desk while Ember looks on, astonished

art.shot: Medium view across the tiny desk.
art.prompt: Sami carefully places Rabbit down on the tiny wooden desk, his face brave and a little wobbly. Ember stands on the other side of the desk, astonished, his spectacles slipping, a tiny wisp of grey sparks above his nose. The tiny desk lamp lights them both. The towering shelves fade into darkness behind. A quiet, important, tender moment.

pages.heading: Rule Four
pages.text:
Ember stared at him. His glasses steamed up.

Then he pulled a tiny notebook from under his wing and wrote something, very fast.

"Rule four," he read out. "When the Keeper retires, he may take one thing home with him."

"Are you retiring?" asked Sami.

"I am now," said Ember, and he picked up Rabbit. "And this is the one thing I'm taking."

Sami laughed so loudly that a pile of umbrellas fell over.

Nobody minded at all.
pages.imageAlt: Ember proudly holding up Rabbit while Sami laughs and a pile of umbrellas topples over behind them

art.shot: Lively medium-wide view of the desk area.
art.prompt: Ember stands on the tiny desk holding Rabbit up proudly in both arms, a tiny blank notebook and pencil beside him, his spectacles steamed up, puffs of happy pink sparks from his nose. Sami is laughing with his head thrown back. Behind them a tall stack of colourful umbrellas topples over in a comic tumble. Joyful, funny, warm lamp-light.

pages.heading: Home
pages.text:
Before they left, Sami put his torch on Ember's desk, wobbly button and all. "For the next Keeper," he said. "It's dark up on those shelves."

At the top of the stairs, Ember gave Rabbit back. "I said I'd take him home," he whispered. "This is home."

Nani was asleep. Sami put Ember on her pillow, right next to her cheek.

Without opening her eyes, Nani reached out and held him close.

"There you are," she murmured. "Where have you been?"

"Waiting," whispered Ember. "But I'm home now."
pages.imageAlt: Nani asleep, holding Ember close against her cheek, as Sami watches from the doorway with Rabbit

art.shot: Soft view across Nani's bed, Sami in the doorway behind.
art.prompt: Nani lies asleep in bed in her lilac nightdress, eyes closed, smiling, holding Ember the small red knitted dragon snugly against her cheek with one hand. Ember's eyes are closed too, and he looks completely content. In the doorway, Sami stands in his rocket pyjamas hugging Rabbit, smiling. Dim amber night-light, moonlight at the window. Deeply tender and calm.

pages.heading: Where Everything Belongs
pages.text:
Back in bed, Sami pulled the covers up to his chin, with Rabbit under one arm.

In the morning, Nani would come down to breakfast holding a small red dragon. She would cry the happy kind of tears. And Sami would pretend he didn't know a thing about it.

But that was the morning.

For now, everything in the house was exactly where it belonged.

And everyone in it was fast asleep.
pages.imageAlt: Sami fast asleep in bed hugging Rabbit, in a dim moonlit room

art.shot: Soft close view from above the bed.
art.prompt: Sami is fast asleep in bed, the duvet pulled up to his chin, Rabbit tucked under one arm with his chewed ear across Sami's cheek. A gentle smile on his face. The room is dim, lit only by soft blue moonlight from the window. Very dim, soft, low-contrast, peaceful and safe.
